findings.title: UnixFileLock opens lock path with O_TRUNC and no O_NOFOLLOW, truncating symlink target
findings.evidence: In _acquire, open_flags = os.O_RDWR | os.O_TRUNC (line 41) is passed to os.open(self.lock_file, open_flags, self._context.mode) (line 44) with no O_NOFOLLOW and no lstat check, so the open follows any symlink planted at the lock path and the kernel truncates the victim file to 0 bytes with the locking process's credentials. The Path(self.lock_file).exists() guard (line 42) also follows the link, and when the target does not exist it adds O_CREAT (line 43), creating/truncating the link target instead. Reachability: any caller doing FileLock(path).acquire() / 'with FileLock(path)' (or AsyncUnixFileLock/BaseAsyncFileLock, which route to this _acquire) reaches the sink; the attacker only needs to create a symlink at the lock path before acquisition, which is the classic precondition for predictable/shared lock paths (e.g. /tmp/myapp.lock). Upstream later fixed exactly this by adding os.O_NOFOLLOW and deferring ftruncate until after flock succeeds (filelock 4.0.12 _unix.py lines 79-85, referencing issue #591), confirming the root cause; SoftFileLock is not affected because its O_CREAT|O_EXCL open refuses to follow an existing symlink (EEXIST).

findings.title: WindowsFileLock opens lock path through reparse points, truncating symlink target
findings.evidence: In _acquire, flags = os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC (lines 22-26) is passed to os.open(self.lock_file, flags, self._context.mode) (line 28) with no reparse-point/symlink check, and the preceding raise_on_not_writable_file (line 20) stats through the link, so os.open follows a symlink planted at the lock path and O_TRUNC zeroes the target file as the locking user. Reachability is gated by link-creation privilege on Windows (SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege/Developer Mode, or an admin-level actor; verified on this host that os.symlink without it fails with WinError 1314), hence low severity. Upstream 4.0.12 replaced this os.open with NtCreateFile + FILE_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT and explicitly rejects reparse points bound to the opened handle (filelock 4.0.12 _windows.py lines 188-190 and 215-271), confirming the same root-cause class was fixed there.
